related_resources.reason: A precise theorem and deformation argument.
Precise definitions of a Palais–Smale sequence and level compactness.

historical_claims.claim: Ambrosetti and Rabinowitz developed the mountain-pass critical-point framework in their 1973 paper.

authorship.scope: Original audio-first lecture and mathematical companion on nonlinear minimax, Palais–Smale compactness, explicit semilinear existence, or critical exponent scaling; inherited manuscripts are unchanged.

prerequisites.reason: Know the exact polynomial mountain-pass example and path minimax idea.
Understand weak and strong convergence of functions.

recommended.reason: Review function norms, basic Hilbert-space ideas and weak limits.
Connect stationary nonlinear boundary problems to introductory differential equations.

background: Single-variable critical points, basic multivariable derivatives, integration by parts, function norms and weak solutions; the new path-minimax arguments are developed from examples.
readiness_checks: State the radius barrier, outside low point, path minimax value and Palais–Smale hypothesis separately.
Explain why minimizing the maximum of paths does not by itself prove existence of a critical function.
